title: I’ve wanted to make this video for a while- but when the show was on ...
transcript: This is a message for the creative team of Lempicka the musical. With your show coming to Seoul, South Korea next year, I want to talk about my experiences seeing your show on Broadway. Because as a Jew, it is maybe one of the most uncomfortable experiences I've ever had in a Broadway theater. And I wanted to explain why so that hopefully this is something that can be addressed in future productions. Because I did really like a lot of the elements of the show, the score in particular. Just for me, it was all overshadowed by the inclusion of the character of Susie Solodar. Now, in the show, Susie is depicted as running this queer nightclub called Lemonical, which is this queer haven during this time of a lot of political unrest and a lot of homophobia being directed at the queer community. She also stands up to the fascist soldiers that come to take over her bar and arrest everyone in it. The only problem is, none of that actually happened in reality. In fact, it was really the opposite. In real life, Susie Solodar did also own a bar, but it was not a queer bar, and in fact, it was very popular with German soldiers during the German occupation. She willingly welcomed these soldiers into her bar. She changed up the programming to appease them, and in fact, after the war, was even convicted as a conspirator. Strangely, there was actually a club called Le Monacle That was not owned by Susie. It was owned by another woman called Lulu de Montparnasse. And just like in the show, it was a lesbian haven and unfortunately, was raided and shut down during the German occupation. And so the thing that made me so uncomfortable was the fact that everyone in the theater was cheering and rooting for this character and leaving the theater thinking, wow, what an amazing person Susie Solodar was, when in reality, she was this deeply complex woman who did a lot of harm. And I think that she could be a really interesting character to explore in a musical, similar to, like, a Fraulein Schneider in cabaret. But the fact that that aspect of her history is not only completely ignored, but actively portrayed as the opposite, I think is ill conceived at best and actively harmful at worst. At the end of the day, it feels like you went out of your way to glorify a woman who I don't think should be glorified, especially when it is such an easy fix. Like, why is her name need to be Susie Solidor, given that the character has so little in common with the real life woman? Just name the character Lulu de Montparnasse, and not only does your musical become more historically accurate, but it also becomes more respectful. This is a musical about one of the most influential Jewish painters of all time, and to use her story as a means To platform and celebrate and glorify an actual convicted Nazi I think is incredibly irresponsible and problematic.
